nodes.content: Infer identifiable direct regulatory edges from incomplete single-cell perturbations despite latent confounding and compensatory feedback.
requirements: Achieve ≥80% direct-edge precision at 30% recall on ground-truth networks containing confounding and feedback.
Specify identifiability assumptions and distinguish unsupported edges from evidence of regulatory absence.

nodes.content: Develop PerturbID: latent-adjusted, feedback-aware intervention models using time-resolved perturbation profiles; distinguish identifiable edges, non-identifiable edges, and powered nulls.
Which perturbation coverage and sampling windows let PerturbID identify direct effects despite latent confounding and compensatory feedback?
Randomized perturbations of ≥70% of regulators plus 2–6-hour sampling let PerturbID attain ≥80% precision at 30% recall on confounded-feedback networks.
Simulate 100 confounded-feedback networks; sweep randomized regulator coverage (30–90%) and sampling (2–24 hours), measuring PerturbID precision at 30% recall.
Across 100 networks, 70% coverage and 2–6-hour sampling achieved 83% precision at 30% recall, versus 65% with 24-hour-only sampling.
Prioritize ≥70% randomized regulator coverage and 2–6-hour sampling for PerturbID; 24-hour-only profiles miss the precision target.
Targeted double perturbations and 1–3-hour sampling yield ≥80% precision at 30% recall with 50% single-knockout coverage.
Benchmark PerturbID on 100 confounded-feedback networks at 50% knockout coverage, comparing uncertainty-targeted double perturbations against random pairs at 1–3 hours.
At 50% coverage, targeted double perturbations reached 74% precision at 30% recall across 100 networks, versus 67% for random pairs.
PerturbID-50 benchmark package: 100 confounded-feedback networks, 50% knockout coverage, targeted and random double-perturbation designs, and 1–3-hour precision evaluation scripts.
Using ≥70% randomized coverage and 2–6-hour sampling, fit latent-adjusted dynamics; classify identifiable edges, unsupported pairs, and powered nulls.
Extend PerturbID-50 simulations to 70% coverage and 2–6-hour sampling; calibrate latent-adjusted edge, unsupported, and powered-null calls.
PerturbID-70 release: calibrated edge calls, unsupported flags, powered-null thresholds, and notebooks specifying intervention, latent-factor, and feedback-identifiability assumptions.
Develop AnchorIV: combine orthogonal CRISPRi guides, early nascent RNA, and negative-control genes to bound direct effects under confounding and feedback.
Benchmark AnchorIV with paired guides and early nascent RNA; test exclusion assumptions, precision at 30% recall, and null-versus-unsupported calibration.
Augment PerturbID-50 networks with paired-guide instruments and nascent RNA; quantify AnchorIV precision, exclusion violations, and powered-null calibration.
AnchorIV-50 report: paired-guide exclusion diagnostics, nascent-RNA edge scores, precision-at-30%-recall curves, and calibrated unsupported-versus-powered-null calls.
Compare AnchorIV-50 and PerturbID-70 on matched networks at respective coverages, measuring precision at 30% recall and powered-null calibration.
On fast-feedback networks, AnchorIV-50 achieved 84% precision at 30% recall versus PerturbID-70’s 67% despite its feedback adjustment.
How much paired-guide off-target activity can AnchorIV tolerate before its fast-feedback precision falls below 80% at 30% recall?
At 50% coverage, paired-guide AnchorIV replaces double perturbations; ≤5% off-target activity preserves ≥80% precision at 30% recall under fast feedback.
Reproduce AnchorIV-50’s 84% fast-feedback baseline; inject 0–20% paired-guide off-target activity and measure precision at 30% recall.
Fast-feedback precision at 30% recall was 84% without off-targets, 81% at 5%, and 76% at 10%.
Benchmark PerturbID-70 against ≤5%-off-target AnchorIV-50 across matched feedback and confounding strata, measuring precision at 30% recall and powered-null specificity.
At 5% off-targets, fast-feedback precision: AnchorIV 81% versus PerturbID 67%; slow-feedback: 79% versus 88%; powered-null specificity: 92% versus 94%.
Use AnchorIV-50 for fast-feedback networks only with ≤5% off-targets; retain PerturbID-70 for slow feedback, where precision reaches 88%.
Develop ClampBound: randomized degron pulses plus nascent-RNA trajectories bound direct effects despite confounding and feedback, distinguishing unsupported from powered nulls.
Which degron pulse lengths and nascent-RNA sampling windows identify direct effects before fast feedback obscures them?
Sweep randomized 15–120-minute degron pulses and 15–180-minute nascent-RNA sampling on PerturbID-50 fast-feedback networks; measure ClampBound precision at 30% recall.
Fast-feedback precision at 30% recall: 86% with 30-minute pulses and 15–60-minute samples; 72% with 120-minute pulses and 180-minute samples.
On fast-feedback networks, 30-minute degron pulses with 15–60-minute sampling sustain ≥80% direct-edge precision at 30% recall.
Validate 30-minute pulses with 15–60-minute sampling on held-out fast-feedback networks; estimate timing robustness and coverage needed for identifiable edges.
On held-out confounded-feedback networks, sweep ClampBound coverage using 30-minute pulses/15–60-minute sampling; retest PerturbID’s 70%-coverage/2–6-hour design at 30% recall.
On held-out fast-feedback networks, 2-hour-only PerturbID-70 reached 82% precision at 30% recall, versus 67% previously; ClampBound reached 85%.
Prioritize ClampBound at 85% fast-feedback precision; reconsider 2-hour-only PerturbID (82%) against AnchorIV (81%) in matched-timing trials.
Run matched-timing trials of prioritized ClampBound, PerturbID, and AnchorIV on confounded-feedback networks; score 30%-recall precision and null calibration.
MatchedTiming-v1 benchmark: matched network splits, intervention schedules, precision-at-30%-recall comparisons, and identifiability and powered-null calibration diagnostics for three methods.
MatchedTiming-v1: ClampBound achieved 86% fast-feedback precision at 30% recall versus PerturbID’s 82% and AnchorIV’s 81%; powered-null specificity was 93%.
When does cell-specific degron efficacy correlated with latent cell state invalidate ClampBound’s direct-edge bounds and powered-null calls?
Inject ρ=0–0.6 degron-efficacy–latent-state correlations into MatchedTiming-v1 while preserving randomized assignment; assess ClampBound precision, bound coverage, and false-absence rate.
At ρ=0.4 efficacy–state correlation, ClampBound precision fell to 73% at 30% recall; nominal 95% bound coverage dropped to 79%.
Use ClampBound only if efficacy–state sensitivity checks retain ≥95% bound coverage; otherwise prefer PerturbID and mark affected edges unsupported.
Develop RescueMap: lineage-matched CRISPRi/CRISPRa rescues with early nascent RNA bound direct effects, separating identifiable edges from unsupported and powered nulls.
How accurately must lineage matching balance latent cell state for CRISPRi/CRISPRa rescue concordance to identify direct edges under fast feedback?
RescueMap replaces pulse-only identification: lineage-state imbalance ≤0.1 SD yields ≥80% precision at 30% recall under fast feedback.
Recreate ρ=0.4 efficacy–state confounding; sweep lineage imbalance 0–0.5 SD in RescueMap rescues, measuring precision at 30% recall.
At ρ=0.4, RescueMap precision at 30% recall was 83% with ≤0.1-SD imbalance, versus 74% at 0.3 SD.
Without ≤0.1-SD lineage balance, RescueMap’s rescue concordance reflects shared latent state and yields ≥10% false direct-edge calls.
Prespecify n35’s 86%-precision ClampBound comparator; measure RescueMap false-edge fractions across 0.1–0.5-SD lineage imbalances at 30% recall.
Under weak confounding (ρ=0.1), RescueMap retained 91% precision at 30% recall despite 0.3-SD lineage imbalance.
Map RescueMap eligibility across ρ=0.1–0.4 confounding and 0.1–0.5-SD lineage imbalance; calibrate edge precision and powered-null validity.
Extend MatchedTiming-v1 across ρ=0.1–0.4 confounding and 0.1–0.5-SD lineage imbalance; measure RescueMap precision at 30% recall and powered-null specificity.
RescueMap eligibility atlas: confounding-by-imbalance precision at 30% recall, powered-null specificity, and thresholds separating supported edges from unsupported pairs.
Stratify the RescueMap atlas by confounding strength; test whether >0.1-SD lineage imbalance consistently causes ≥10% false direct-edge calls.
Under strong confounding (ρ=0.4), 0.2-SD lineage imbalance caused 12% false edges at 30% recall; weak-confounding exceptions remain.
Can negative-control genes estimate confounding strength well enough to relax RescueMap’s 0.1-SD balance requirement without inflating false edges?
Negative controls estimate ρ within 0.05; inferred ρ≤0.1 permits 0.3-SD lineage imbalance with ≥80% precision at 30% recall.
Fit negative-control ρ estimates using RescueMap atlas’s weak/strong-confounding strata; test ±0.05 error and precision at 30% recall, 0.3-SD imbalance.
Negative-control ρ estimates were within 0.05 in 92% of networks; selected ρ≤0.1 cases achieved 88% precision at 30% recall.

Prespecify RescueMap eligibility: randomized guides, ≤0.1-SD imbalance or negative-control-estimated ρ≤0.1 at ≤0.3-SD imbalance; validate 30%-recall precision and unsupported-versus-powered-null calls.
Apply atlas-based RescueMap eligibility to 100 held-out confounded-feedback networks; measure precision at 30% recall and powered-null specificity.
MatchedTiming-v2 extends v1 with RescueMap eligibility gates, 100 held-out networks, 30%-recall precision, powered-null specificity, and explicit unsupported-edge labels.
Stress-test MatchedTiming-v2’s eligible RescueMap calls at ρ=0.4 efficacy–state correlation; measure precision at 30% recall and powered-null specificity.
At ρ=0.4, ≤0.1-SD-matched RescueMap achieved 83% precision at 30% recall and 94% powered-null specificity on MatchedTiming-v2.
Choose RescueMap with ≤0.1-SD balance under strong confounding or control-verified weak confounding; otherwise use diagnostic-qualified AnchorIV, PerturbID, or ClampBound.
